sentences.text: [serious] About $558,100 in paper profit, more than a couple can take tax-free.
sentences.spoken: [serious] About five hundred fifty-eight thousand one hundred dollars in paper profit, more than a couple can take tax-free.

sentences.text: That's Rosa and Frank, an illustrative Phoenix couple who bought in 2000, if their home rose like the average.
sentences.spoken: That's Rosa and Frank, an illustrative Phoenix couple who bought in two thousand, if their home rose like the average.

sentences.text: You'll know, city by city, the 2000 price where a home that rose like its metro area's average passes that cap, to check yours against.
sentences.spoken: You'll know, city by city, the two thousand price where a home that rose like its metro area's average passes that cap, to check yours against.

sentences.text: It's a line for a home like the average: not anyone's tax bill, and not a reason to sell or keep.
sentences.spoken: It's a line for a home like the average: not anyone's tax bill, and not a reason to sell or keep.

sentences.text: This is US only: federal tax, with state taxes not modeled.
sentences.spoken: This is U.S. only: federal tax, with state taxes not modeled.

sentences.text: Every couple here is illustrative, and assumed to have owned and lived in the home two of the five years before selling.
sentences.spoken: Every couple here is illustrative, and assumed to have owned and lived in the home two of the five years before selling.

sentences.text: And every price you'll see is history, not a forecast.
sentences.spoken: And every price you'll see is history, not a forecast.

sentences.text: When you sell, your gain is the sale price, less what you paid, and less what you spent improving the place.
sentences.spoken: When you sell, your gain is the sale price, less what you paid, and less what you spent improving the place.

sentences.text: A married couple filing jointly can leave up to $500,000 of that gain off their taxes, and a single seller can leave out $250,000.
sentences.spoken: A married couple filing jointly can leave up to five hundred thousand dollars of that gain off their taxes, and a single seller can leave out two hundred fifty thousand dollars.

sentences.text: Those caps took effect in May 1997.
sentences.spoken: Those caps took effect in May nineteen ninety-seven.

sentences.text: They are plain dollar amounts, and they haven't changed since.
sentences.spoken: They are plain dollar amounts, and they haven't changed since.

sentences.text: Back to Frank and Rosa.
sentences.spoken: Back to Frank and Rosa.

sentences.text: In 2000, they paid $200,000 for a house in Phoenix.
sentences.spoken: In two thousand, they paid two hundred thousand dollars for a house in Phoenix.

sentences.text: Their kids have moved out, and on weekends they both look at smaller places.
sentences.spoken: Their kids have moved out, and on weekends they both look at smaller places.

sentences.text: Whenever selling comes up, Frank says the same thing: at least the profit is tax-free.
sentences.spoken: Whenever selling comes up, Frank says the same thing: at least the profit is tax-free.

sentences.text: [thoughtful] Is it? Has their gain passed the cap?
sentences.spoken: [thoughtful] Is it? Has their gain passed the cap?

sentences.text: We can't see their house, so we let its value rise exactly like the Phoenix area home price index from the Federal Housing Finance Agency, an average of many sales.
sentences.spoken: We can't see their house, so we let its value rise exactly like the Phoenix area home price index from the Federal Housing Finance Agency, an average of many sales.

sentences.text: We follow it quarter by quarter, from 2000 to the second quarter of 2026, the latest data.
sentences.spoken: We follow it quarter by quarter, from two thousand to the second quarter of twenty twenty-six, the latest data.

sentences.text: Here's the cap: a flat line at $500,000, the same in every quarter.
sentences.spoken: Here's the cap: a flat line at five hundred thousand dollars, the same in every quarter.

sentences.text: And here's their gain on paper, for a home that rose like the average: the $200,000, grown with the index, less the $200,000 they paid.
sentences.spoken: And here's their gain on paper, for a home that rose like the average: the two hundred thousand dollars, grown with the index, less the two hundred thousand dollars they paid.

sentences.text: For most of these years, it sits well under the line.
sentences.spoken: For most of these years, it sits well under the line.

sentences.text: Then, in the second quarter of 2022, it crosses.
sentences.spoken: Then, in the second quarter of twenty twenty-two, it crosses.

sentences.text: It slips back under for a while.
sentences.spoken: It slips back under for a while.

sentences.text: From the second quarter of 2023, it has stayed above.
sentences.spoken: From the second quarter of twenty twenty-three, it has stayed above.

sentences.text: [serious] So, on paper, if their home rose like the Phoenix average, this is the gain from the opening.
sentences.spoken: [serious] So, on paper, if their home rose like the Phoenix average, this is the gain from the opening.

sentences.text: That's past the cap.
sentences.spoken: That's past the cap.

sentences.text: Phoenix area prices are now almost 3.8 times their 2000 level.
sentences.spoken: Phoenix area prices are now almost three point eight times their two thousand level.

sentences.text: And it's a gain, not a tax bill: improvements and selling costs would both shrink it.
sentences.spoken: And it's a gain, not a tax bill: improvements and selling costs would both shrink it.

sentences.text: The cap stood still while their gain climbed past it.
sentences.spoken: The cap stood still while their gain climbed past it.

sentences.text: So is Phoenix unusual, or would the same thing happen in other cities?
sentences.spoken: So is Phoenix unusual, or would the same thing happen in other cities?

sentences.text: First, why is the line flat?
sentences.spoken: First, why is the line flat?

sentences.text: The cap is written as a plain dollar amount, and it has never been adjusted.
sentences.spoken: The cap is written as a plain dollar amount, and it has never been adjusted.

sentences.text: If $500,000 from May 1997 had kept up with consumer prices, it would be about $1,046,000 in August 2026 dollars.
sentences.spoken: If five hundred thousand dollars from May nineteen ninety-seven had kept up with consumer prices, it would be about one million forty-six thousand dollars in August twenty twenty-six dollars.

sentences.text: It's everyday prices, not house prices, but it shows why a cap that never moves covers less and less of a long-held home's gain.
sentences.spoken: It's everyday prices, not house prices, but it shows why a cap that never moves covers less and less of a long-held home's gain.

sentences.text: Now run the same replay in 12 big metro areas: illustrative couples, each paying $200,000 in 2000 for a home that rose like its metro area's average.
sentences.spoken: Now run the same replay in twelve big metro areas: illustrative couples, each paying two hundred thousand dollars in two thousand for a home that rose like its metro area's average.

sentences.text: By the second quarter of 2026, the gain is past the cap in 5 of them.
sentences.spoken: By the second quarter of twenty twenty-six, the gain is past the cap in five of them.

sentences.text: Los Angeles, San Diego, Seattle, Miami and Phoenix.
sentences.spoken: Los Angeles, San Diego, Seattle, Miami and Phoenix.

sentences.text: Now give every couple $300,000 instead.
sentences.spoken: Now give every couple three hundred thousand dollars instead.

sentences.text: This time, for homes that rose like their metro area's average, the gain is past the cap in 11 of the 12.
sentences.spoken: This time, for homes that rose like their metro area's average, the gain is past the cap in eleven of the twelve.

sentences.text: Boston, New York, Denver, Dallas and both Bay Area markets join the first five.
sentences.spoken: Boston, New York, Denver, Dallas and both Bay Area markets join the first five.

sentences.text: Only Chicago hasn't reached the cap, at either price.
sentences.spoken: Only Chicago hasn't reached the cap, at either price.

sentences.text: [curious] And crossing isn't always a one-way trip.
sentences.spoken: [curious] And crossing isn't always a one-way trip.

sentences.text: In Miami, a $300,000 home that rose like the average first passed the cap in the fourth quarter of 2006.
sentences.spoken: In Miami, a three hundred thousand dollars home that rose like the average first passed the cap in the fourth quarter of two thousand six.

sentences.text: Then it fell back under, and has only stayed above since the second quarter of 2019.
sentences.spoken: Then it fell back under, and has only stayed above since the second quarter of twenty nineteen.

sentences.text: Being past the line once, on paper, didn't mean staying past it.
sentences.spoken: Being past the line once, on paper, didn't mean staying past it.

sentences.text: So Phoenix isn't unusual, and it isn't only the coasts: Dallas and Denver crossed too.
sentences.spoken: So Phoenix isn't unusual, and it isn't only the coasts: Dallas and Denver crossed too.

sentences.text: So flip the question.
sentences.spoken: So flip the question.

sentences.text: What 2000 purchase price would put a home that rose like its metro area's average exactly at the cap now?
sentences.spoken: What two thousand purchase price would put a home that rose like its metro area's average exactly at the cap now?

sentences.text: In Phoenix, for a home that rose like the average, that price is about $179,200.
sentences.spoken: In Phoenix, for a home that rose like the average, that price is about one hundred seventy-nine thousand two hundred dollars.

sentences.text: Rosa and Frank paid more than that, and that's why their line crossed.
sentences.spoken: Rosa and Frank paid more than that, and that's why their line crossed.

sentences.text: Below that price, a Phoenix home is still under the cap; above it, it's over.
sentences.spoken: Below that price, a Phoenix home is still under the cap; above it, it's over.

sentences.text: Do that for all 12 metro areas, each for a home that rose like its metro area's average, and you get a ladder of prices.
sentences.spoken: Do that for all twelve metro areas, each for a home that rose like its metro area's average, and you get a ladder of prices.

sentences.text: Miami sits at the bottom of the ladder, and Chicago at the top.
sentences.spoken: Miami sits at the bottom of the ladder, and Chicago at the top.

sentences.text: The faster an area's prices rose, the lower its rung: Miami's rose the most, Chicago's the least.
sentences.spoken: The faster an area's prices rose, the lower its rung: Miami's rose the most, Chicago's the least.

sentences.text: Every city except Chicago sits under $300,000.
sentences.spoken: Every city except Chicago sits under three hundred thousand dollars.

sentences.text: That's the cap, read a third way: not as a flat line, but as a price paid in 2000 that anyone can look up.
sentences.spoken: That's the cap, read a third way: not as a flat line, but as a price paid in two thousand that anyone can look up.

sentences.text: So, back to the opening question: is selling a home bought in 2000 still fully tax-free?
sentences.spoken: So, back to the opening question: is selling a home bought in two thousand still fully tax-free?

sentences.text: [serious] For Rosa and Frank, if their house rose like its metro area's average, not fully: part of their gain sits above the cap.
sentences.spoken: [serious] For Rosa and Frank, if their house rose like its metro area's average, not fully: part of their gain sits above the cap.

sentences.text: For you, it may come down to one comparison: your 2000 price against your city's rung.
sentences.spoken: For you, it may come down to one comparison: your two thousand price against your city's rung.

sentences.text: Above that rung, a home like that has already passed the cap. Below it, it hasn't.
sentences.spoken: Above that rung, a home like that has already passed the cap. Below it, it hasn't.

sentences.text: Below the rung isn't proof of no tax, and above it isn't proof of a large one. The video measures one line; it says nothing about what anyone does next.
sentences.spoken: Below the rung isn't proof of no tax, and above it isn't proof of a large one. The video measures one line; it says nothing about what anyone does next.

sentences.text: Your side of it is what you paid plus improvements, which count toward what the gain is measured from.
sentences.spoken: Your side of it is what you paid plus improvements, which count toward what the gain is measured from.

sentences.text: Selling costs, like agent fees, come off the gain too.
sentences.spoken: Selling costs, like agent fees, come off the gain too.

sentences.text: Outside these cities, the national index puts the line, for a home like the average, at about $243,500.
sentences.spoken: Outside these cities, the national index puts the line, for a home like the average, at about two hundred forty-three thousand five hundred dollars.

sentences.text: For a single seller, with the $250,000 cap, the national line is about $121,700.
sentences.spoken: For a single seller, with the two hundred fifty thousand dollars cap, the national line is about one hundred twenty-one thousand seven hundred dollars.

sentences.text: None of this is anyone's tax bill.
sentences.spoken: None of this is anyone's tax bill.

sentences.text: Gain above the cap is taxed as a long-term capital gain, since the home was held more than a year, at a rate that depends on income and state.
sentences.spoken: Gain above the cap is taxed as a long-term capital gain, since the home was held more than a year, at a rate that depends on income and state.

sentences.text: And the average is not your home: your street, your remodel and your purchase month can put you far from your rung.
sentences.spoken: And the average is not your home: your street, your remodel and your purchase month can put you far from your rung.

sentences.text: The line is a measurement, not a next step; this video doesn't weigh selling, keeping or waiting.
sentences.spoken: The line is a measurement, not a next step; this video doesn't weigh selling, keeping or waiting.

sentences.text: How we built this is on screen and in the description.
sentences.spoken: How we built this is on screen and in the description.

sentences.text: The price indexes are revised every quarter, so these lines can move a little with the next release.
sentences.spoken: The price indexes are revised every quarter, so these lines can move a little with the next release.

sentences.text: This is history, not a forecast: where prices went from 2000 to the second quarter of 2026, not where they, or the cap, go next.
sentences.spoken: This is history, not a forecast: where prices went from two thousand to the second quarter of twenty twenty-six, not where they, or the cap, go next.

sentences.text: [thoughtful] The cap is still the same flat line it was in 1997.
sentences.spoken: [thoughtful] The cap is still the same flat line it was in nineteen ninety-seven.

sentences.text: What moved is the house underneath it.
sentences.spoken: What moved is the house underneath it.
